## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace of the four scaffolded packages under `packages/` (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (index row count × request rate; not yet measured); measured per quarter by Stage 3 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression). One track: each outcome consumes the one before it.

Order: stages follow your ranking O1 → O2 → O3, with one divergence. Stage 4 handles 10-K and 8-K on a single quarter of submissions before Stage 5 downloads the full history. Stage 4 is cheap, and its answer may narrow Stage 5's download to 10-K and 8-K submissions only. That could cut weeks of downloading.

## Open questions

1. Submission history range for Stage 5. The choices are every submission since 1993, a bounded range, or only the form types Stage 4 shows are needed. The default is to decide at the resume after Stage 4, from its measured cost. Stages 1–4 do not depend on it.
2. Deployment platform for Stage 7. The ADR's Azure design (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage) is Proposed and serves as background. It is not a choice yet. The default is to settle it in Stage 7's brainstorming. Nothing before Stage 7 depends on it.
3. Scope note. The background spec §2.2 puts filing-document downloads out of scope. Your progression puts them in (O2, O3), and your words govern. The spec's index design (§4) remains background for Stages 1, 2 and 6.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: One quarter of index, end to end
      Objective: Load one real quarterly master index and one real daily master index into a filing-index table on local disk.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table schema and loader that later stages extend; an SEC request path that sends an identifying User-Agent and stays under the request target; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: the table holds every row of the chosen quarter's master.idx and the daily file, with no duplicate rows from their overlap. The findings file records the measured bytes, row counts, download time, parse time and request rate of the real run.
      Leaves out: full history and daily continuation (Stage 2); legacy-format coverage (Stage 2); manifest, raw-snapshot replay, reconciliation and versioned publication (Stage 6); fixture validation suite (Stage 6); scheduling, deployment and monitoring (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Full index history and daily catch-up
      Objective: Extend the table to every quarter in range and to every daily index through today, with a rerun that picks up new daily files.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1's table, loader and SEC request path
      Produces: a complete filing-index table that later stages read to select submissions; a gap report; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: every quarter in range and every listed daily file is either in the table or named in the gap report. A second run a day later adds only the new daily files. The findings file records the measured cost of the full backfill.
      Leaves out: manifest, replay, reconciliation of later quarterly changes and withdrawals, and versioned publication (Stage 6); fixture validation suite (Stage 6); scheduled runs (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Submissions for one quarter
      Objective: Download the submissions that one quarter's index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 2's filing-index table; Stage 1's SEC request path
      Produces: submissions on disk for one quarter, located by index row; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: each of the quarter's index rows maps to a downloaded submission or to a recorded failure. The findings file records the measured files, bytes, time per filing, and a full-history extrapolation.
      Leaves out: full submission history and resumable long runs (Stage 5); download manifest and provenance (Stage 6); scheduling (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: 10-K and 8-K on one quarter
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of Stage 3's submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 3's submissions on disk and their index rows
      Produces: extracted main documents for the quarter's 10-K and 8-K filings; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-4-findings.md
      Exit: every 10-K and 8-K in the quarter has an extracted main document or a recorded failure reason. The findings file records the measured counts, extraction time, failure rate, and the share of submissions that are 10-K or 8-K.
      Leaves out: full-history extraction (Stage 5); extraction provenance and replay (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Full submission history with 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Download submissions across the range settled at the resume (Open question 1), and run 10-K and 8-K handling over them.
      Outcomes: O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 2–4 and their findings files
      Produces: submissions and extracted 10-K and 8-K main documents across the settled range; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-5-findings.md
      Exit: every in-range index row selected for download has a submission or a recorded failure. An interrupted run resumes without downloading again what it already has. Every 10-K and 8-K among them has an extracted main document or a recorded failure. The findings file records the measured cost of the full run.
      Leaves out: manifest, provenance and replay (Stage 6); scheduling and monitoring (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Provenance, replay, reconciliation and validation
      Objective: Make every output traceable to retained source bytes, rebuildable without new SEC requests, and reconciled against later quarterly changes.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–5's tables, files and loaders
      Produces: a manifest of sources, snapshots and processing versions; versioned publication of the filing-index table; quarterly reconciliation; a fixture validation suite
      Exit: a parser-version change rebuilds the table and extractions from retained bytes with zero SEC requests. A changed quarterly file records its additions, updates and withdrawals without silently dropping rows. The fixture suite covers the historical index formats in range and runs in CI without network access.
      Leaves out: scheduled operation, deployment and alerting (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling, deployment and monitoring
      Objective: Run daily ingestion and periodic reconciliation on a schedule, on the platform settled in Open question 2, with alerts and runbooks.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 6's manifest, publication and reconciliation
      Produces: deployed scheduled jobs, alerts and runbooks
      Exit: scheduled daily and reconciliation runs execute on their own. A missed run catches up and is shown in its run report. A failure raises an alert.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
